title: Two Controllers Detected When One Controller Connected
body: ### Tested versions 4.5 stable ### System information Godot v4.5.stable - Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS 22.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated Quadro T1000 (nvidia; 580.126.09) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9750H CPU @ 2.60GHz (12 threads) - 30.99 GiB memory ### Issue description Connecting to Input.joy_connection_changed results in two events for the same XBox controller connection event. Verifying with Input.get_connected_joypads() also confirms that there are two joypads detected by the system, despite a single joypad being connected to my computer. Debug logs show that the two controllers are being detected as slightly different devices by name, but share all other identification features. Console output: ``` Guid: 050018dc5e0400008e02000030110000 Info: { "raw_name": "Xbox 360 Controller", "vendor_id": "1118", "product_id": "654", "xinput_index": "0" } name: Xbox 360 Controller Guid: 0500a18a5e0400008e02000030110000 Info: { "raw_name": "Xbox 360 Controller", "vendor_id": "1118", "product_id": "654" } name: Microsoft Xbox One Elite 2 ``` Debug code used to produce console output ``` var guid = Input.get_joy_guid(device) var device_info = Input.get_joy_info(device) var device_name = Input.get_joy_name(device) print("Guid: ", guid, " Info: ", device_info, " name: ", device_name) ``` I can confirm through my bluetooth settings that there is only one controller connected to the computer I have not tried with other controllers - only XBox ### Steps to reproduce To view multiple controllers Create a node and in the _ready() method include the following code: ``` var controllers = Input.get_connected_joypads() for controller in controllers: var guid = Input.get_joy_guid(controller) var device_info = Input.get_joy_info(controller) var device_name = Input.get_joy_name(controller) print("Guid: ", guid, " Info: ", device_info, " name: ", device_name) ``` Connect your XBox controller, then run the game. Console will clearly show two devices as connected. To view mutliple connection events from the same connection: In the _ready() method connect to the Input.joy_connection_changed signal ``` Input.joy_connection_changed.connect(_on_joy_connection_changed) ``` Print debug information in the on_joy_connection_changed method ``` func _on_joy_connection_changed(device: int, connected: bool) -> void: var guid = Input.get_joy_guid(device) var device_info = Input.get_joy_info(device) var device_name = Input.get_joy_name(device) print("Guid: ", guid, " Info: ", device_info, " name: ", device_name) ``` Begin with no controller connected. Run the game Connect the controller with the game running Observe the output - two debug lines will be printed ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
